statement: Whenever longest_special_path(edges, nums) returns a result r, r is a vector of length 2 and r[0] = L and r[1] = M, where: root the tree at node 0; a node a is an ancestor of b when a lies on the unique simple path from 0 to b (allowing a=b); for such a,b, P(a,b) is the vertex sequence on the unique simple path from a to b, wt(a,b) is the sum of the edge lengths between consecutive vertices of P(a,b), and sz(a,b) is the number of vertices in P(a,b); P(a,b) is special when every value occurs at most twice among nums on P(a,b) and at most one value occurs exactly twice; S is the set of all pairs (a,b) such that a is an ancestor of b and P(a,b) is special; L = max over (a,b) in S of wt(a,b), and M = min over (a,b) in S with wt(a,b)=L of sz(a,b).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The inputs satisfy the problem constraints: 2 <= n <= 50000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[i] has length 3 and, writing edges[i] = [u,v,w], we have 0 <= u < n, 0 <= v < n, and 1 <= w <= 1000; the undirected graph on vertices 0,...,n-1 with these n-1 weighted edges is a tree; and 0 <= nums[j] <= 50000 for every 0 <= j < n.
